questions.question: What is the value of ( \(\frac{7}{8}\) × 2.4) ÷ 0.6?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of (\(\frac{7}{8}\) × 2.4) ÷ 0.6?
questions.solution:
⇒ \(2.4 = \frac{24}{10} = \frac{12}{5}\) ⇒ \(0.6 = \frac{6}{10} = \frac{3}{5}\)

⇒ \(\left(\frac{7}{8} \times \frac{12}{5}\right) \div \frac{3}{5}\)⇒ \(\frac{7 \times 12}{8 \times 5} \times \frac{5}{3}\)

⇒ \(\frac{7 \times 3}{2 \times 5} \times \frac{5}{3}\) ⇒ 3.5

questions.solution:
⇒ (√7 + √3)² - 2√21

⇒ (7 + 3 + 2×√7×√3) - 2√21

⇒ 10 + 2√21 - 2√21

⇒ 10

questions.question: Aman needed ₹30,000 for a start-up and split the sum between two private lenders under simple-interest terms: Lender A charges 9 % p.a. (simple interest) Lender B charges 6 % p.a. (simple interest) Aman kept both loans exactly 4 years and then made a single lump-sum payment that settled only the accumulated interest, which came to ₹9,600. After preparing his books of account, Aman discovered that he interchanged the principal amounts taken from the two lenders, his four-year interest outgo would have been ₹1,200 less than what he actually paid. How much of the original ₹30,000 did Aman borrow at 9 % p.a. from Lender A?

questions.question: A shopkeeper marked an item 50% above its cost price. He then offered two successive discounts of 10% and 20% to a customer. If he made a profit of ₹80, at what price did he sell the item to that customer?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marked an item 50% above its cost price. He then offered two successive discounts of 10% and 20% to a customer. If he made a profit of ₹80, at what price did he sell the item to that customer?
questions.solution:
Let Cost Price = 100

⇒ Marked Price = 100 × 150 ÷ 100 = 150

⇒ After 10% discount = 150 × 90 ÷ 100 = 135

⇒ After 20% discount = 135 × 80 ÷ 100 = 108

⇒ Profit on CP 100 = 108 − 100 = 8

⇒ If profit 8 corresponds to 80, So 1 corresponds to 10

⇒ Required Selling Price = 108 × 10 = 1080

questions.question: A is three times as efficient as a worker than B, which allows A to complete a job in 60 days less than B. If they work together, they can finish the job in:
questions.questionHtml: A is three times as efficient as a worker than B, which allows A to complete a job in 60 days less than B. If they work together, they can finish the job in:
questions.solution:
Efficiency of A : B = 3 : 1 ⇒ Time of A : Time of B = 1 : 3.

Let Time of A = x, Time of B = 3x ⇒ 3x − x = 60 ⇒ 2x = 60 ⇒ x = 30.

Time of A = 30 days, Time of B = 90 days ⇒ Total work = LCM(30, 90) = 90 units.

Rate of A = 90 ÷ 30 = 3 units/day, Rate of B = 90 ÷ 90 = 1 unit/day ⇒ Combined rate = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day.

Time together = 90 ÷ 4 = 22.5 days.

questions.question: A cyclist has to cover a distance of 80 km. After cycling for 4 hours and 48 minutes, he finds that he has completed \(\frac{4}{5}\) th of the total distance. What is his speed in km/h?
questions.questionHtml: A cyclist has to cover a distance of 80 km. After cycling for 4 hours and 48 minutes, he finds that he has completed \(\frac{4}{5}\) th of the total distance. What is his speed in km/h?
questions.solution:
⇒ Distance covered = 80 × 4 ÷ 5 = 64 km

⇒ Time in hours = 4 + 48 ÷ 60 = 4.8 hours

⇒ Speed = 64 ÷ 4.8 = 13.33 km/h

questions.question: A vertical pole of height H stands on the ground. From a point P on the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the pole is 60°. From a different point Q, located 10 meters away from point P (directly along the line extending from the base of the pole), the angle of elevation to the top of the pole is 30°.What is the height of the pole?
questions.questionHtml: A vertical pole of height H stands on the ground. From a point P on the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the pole is 60°. From a different point Q, located 10 meters away from point P (directly along the line extending from the base of the pole), the angle of elevation to the top of the pole is 30°.What is the height of the pole?
questions.solution:
Let distance of P from pole = x

⇒ tan 60º = H ÷ x ⇒ √3 = H ÷ x ⇒ H = x√3

⇒ tan 30º = H ÷ (x + 10) ⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = H ÷ (x + 10) ⇒ H = (x + 10) ÷ √3

⇒ x√3 = (x + 10) ÷ √3 ⇒ x × 3 = x + 10 ⇒ 3x = x + 10 ⇒ 2x = 10 ⇒ x = 5

⇒ H = 5√3

questions.question: If the perimeter of a regular octagon is 80 cm, what is the side length?
questions.questionHtml: If the perimeter of a regular octagon is 80 cm, what is the side length?
questions.solution:
Perimeter = 80 cm, Number of sides = 8

Side length = 80 ÷ 8

⇒ Side length = 10 cm

questions.question: If the lateral surface area of a prism is 240 cm² and height is 8 cm, what is the perimeter of the base?
questions.questionHtml: If the lateral surface area of a prism is 240 cm² and height is 8 cm, what is the perimeter of the base?
questions.solution:
LSA = Perimeter of base × Height

Perimeter of base = 240 ÷ 8

Perimeter of base = 30 cm

questions.question: If two circles are touching internally how many common tangents do they have?
questions.questionHtml: If two circles are touching internally how many common tangents do they have?
questions.solution:
Given: Two circles touch internally, one lies inside the other, and they touch at exactly one point.

Number of common tangents depends on the relative position of the circles.

When circles touch internally, only one common tangent exists at the point of contact.

questions.question: A sector of a circle with radius 6 cm has a central angle of 60°. What is the area of the corresponding segment?
questions.questionHtml: A sector of a circle with radius 6 cm has a central angle of 60°. What is the area of the corresponding segment?
questions.solution:
⇒ Area of sector = (60 ÷ 360) × π × 62 = (1 ÷ 6) × π × 36 = 6π sq. cm

⇒ Area of triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × 6 × 6 × sin(60°) = (1 ÷ 2) × 36 × (√3 ÷ 2) = 9√3 sq. cm

⇒ Area of segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle = 6π − 9√3 sq. cm
